verdict: key consistent: signs = letters = 40 with the twelve word groups matching the twelve words exactly; every repeated shape takes one letter except S6, which is ب four times and ي once (سيف), the same skeleton; ل is written S1 seven times and S9 once. The record's 43 was the segmenter's (it counted the row-12 divider stem as a sign and split two signs).
notes: Rows 11-13 of image 0084_0030 and row 1 of image 0084_0031 (13v l.1), recorded here as line 14. Signs by eye 11+11+9+9 = 40 = letters; no surplus, no drop, so the record's 3 surplus signs are segmenter artefacts (on row 12 the divider stem with its dots is boxed as sign 10). Word groups by three-dot dividers: 3|3|4|3(over the line end)|3|4|3(over the line end)|3|4|3(over the line end)|3|4, i.e. exactly the words. The verse repeats لكل four times and طرف twice, so the table is well tested for those letters: لكل is S1 S2 S1 three times and S9 S2 S1 once. S6 for ي in سيف (otherwise ب) fits the compiler's remark that the text is 'seven similar words of strange build': the encipherer may have keyed by letter skeleton for this letter, or slipped; one instance only.
